clues: This city sits in the south centre of its land, in East Africa. It is the great trade hub for the whole east of the continent.
This city sits close to the equator, yet its nights are cool. High ground cools the air, and the year splits into a wet time and a dry time.
This town began in 1898 as a depot for the rail line. By 1907 it had grown to take the place of the old port as capital.
This is the only capital city in the world with a national park inside its bounds. You can leave the streets and step straight into wild park land.
The Parliament Buildings of Kenya stand in this city. The State House and the Supreme Court stand here too.
